title: Continuous-Time Counterfactual Quantile Learning for Risk-Sensitive Policy Optimization

problem.claim: The paper studies continuous-time counterfactual quantile learning for risk-sensitive policy optimization.

gap.claim: Existing causal inference methods commonly focus on expectation-based or discrete-time counterfactual reasoning, which may fail to capture fine-grained temporal dynamics and critical risks.

contributions.claim: CT-CQL models full counterfactual outcome distributions with stochastic differential equations governed by the Fokker–Planck equation.
CT-CQL uses a minimax objective to minimize Fokker–Planck residuals under adversarial perturbations and a double-robust AIPW loss to mitigate confounding bias.
CT-CQL optimizes intervention strategies for expected utility subject to real-world budget and safety constraints.

stated_novelty.claim: The proposed framework is built upon a novel identification theory.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on widely used benchmarks and the MIMIC-III dataset are reported to demonstrate validation and superiority of CT-CQL.
The project implementation is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper formulates continuous-time counterfactual quantile learning for risk-sensitive policy optimization.
The motivating applications involve high-frequency, continuously evolving data, while existing causal methods often use expectation-based or discrete-time reasoning.
Such methods may miss fine-grained temporal dynamics and risks that are not reflected in average outcomes.
CT-CQL combines a stated novel identification theory, SDE/FPE distribution modeling, adversarial minimax robustness, and a double-robust AIPW loss.
The framework targets constrained robust policy optimization and is evaluated on benchmarks and MIMIC-III.

source_observation.claim: Average outcomes can conceal severe episodes in continuously evolving settings.

interpretation.claim: Risk-sensitive decision systems may need temporal and distributional counterfactual modeling rather than expectation-only evaluation.

application.claim: Applications with high-frequency observations and safety-critical tail events may benefit from continuous-time, quantile-aware policy optimization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is necessary or effective outside the reported application settings and datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the identification assumptions or theory details.
